critical_code_review_comments: MasterHomepageAvatar.jsx is now ~697 lines — right at the 700-line guideline. The two new listener additions (onTimeUpdate ~340, onPlay ~355) and the immediate-state-sync block (~374) are correctly placed inside the single listener-effect, so removeEventListener cleanup is symmetric. No leaks.

The immediate-state-sync block at ~374 uses setTimeout(...,0) to defer one tick so React commits the scene-change setBuffering(true) before clearing it — correct ordering. The 800ms safety in scene-change effect (~214) is a redundant belt-and-braces for cache-hit scenarios; both can fire and the second is a no-op (idempotent setBuffering(false)). Acceptable.

lastSeenTime is captured in closure scope of the listener effect (line ~340) and resets to -1 only on listener re-mount (not on scene change). For sceneIdx=N→N+1 transitions, currentTime resets to 0 which is < lastSeenTime, so the first tick after scene-change won't trigger a force-clear — but that's fine because canplay/loadeddata/playing fire fresh on the new src and the safety setTimeout in the scene-change effect covers the cached-hit path. Minor: could reset lastSeenTime in the scene-change effect for cleaner semantics, but no functional bug.

The `play` event listener at ~355 calls only setPaused(false) — does NOT clear buffering. This is intentional (play fires before first frame, frame may still need to decode), and onPlaying / onTimeUpdate are the authoritative buffering-clear signals. Worth a one-line code comment to document why setBuffering is deliberately omitted from onPlay.

rca_of_the_issue: User reported on iteration 98 follow-up: laptop/desktop showed permanent 'BUFFERING…' overlay over a clearly-playing avatar (mouth mid-speech in screenshot). Root cause: with `autoplay` set, browser starts decoding the moment <video> mounts; `play` and `playing` events can fire BEFORE React's listener-effect attaches (effect runs after first paint). Result: setBuffering(false) from onPlaying never executes → overlay stuck. Iter 99 fix verified: (1) NEW timeupdate listener authoritatively force-clears buffering whenever currentTime advances by >0.05s, (2) NEW play listener fires earlier than playing for optimistic UI, (3) NEW immediate state-sync block at listener-attach time — if v.readyState>=2 OR !v.paused after attachment, schedules setTimeout(0) that clears buffering and triggers tryPlay, (4) scene-change effect arms an 800ms safety re-check for cache-hit scenarios from the desktop preloader. All four mechanisms confirmed in source (lines 214, 326-358, 374-391). Verification: 4/4 samples at 1440x900 had buffering_visible=false; 0 samples had buffering=true persistent. Bug pathology does not reproduce.
